what: Drop the multiplex and adopt five principles for future recreation planning

what: Approve the 2017 financial plan in principle (includes recreation spending and the performing arts centre)
for: Goertzen; Fehr; Siemens; a Councillor Penner (mover)
reasons_against: Both opposed the $24M performing arts centre and its borrowing, not the recreation operating budget.

what: Buy 40 acres of the Fly-In Golf Club for $500,000 and lease it back for $1 a year
result: Carried (count not announced; stated positions imply 4-3)
for: Fehr; Siemens; Goertzen; one Councillor Penner
reasons_against: A bailout dressed up as a land deal, same amount as the refused grant, no appraisal, $1 lease, unfair to non-profits and businesses refused grants, closed-door handling.
source: transcript 2017-12-05 (stated positions; tally not read out)

what: Adopt the 2018 Financial Plan (included the Park Hill connector pathway; no grant for the Pat Porter seniors' centre)
for: Cari Penner; John Fehr; Jac Siemens; Chris Goertzen
against: Michael Zwaagstra; Susan Penner; Earl Funk
reasons_against: Mainly the golf-course land purchase and closed-door process; Funk contrasted it with the seniors' centre's unanswered public grant request.

what: Amendment to cut the Clearspring Greens pathway to unlit limestone to lower residents' cost

what: First and second readings of By-Law 2132 (Clearspring Greens pathway local improvement)
for: Damian Penner; Michael Zwaagstra; Susan Penner; Bill Hiebert; Earl Funk
reasons_against: Cost to the 146 homes (~$1,000 a year for 5 years) too high; residents should not pay most of a connecting pathway.

what: Remove pathway lighting from the local improvement and fund it from city reserves
for: Michael Zwaagstra; Bill Hiebert; Susan Penner; Damian Penner; Jake Hiebert; Earl Funk

what: Conditional use CU-2022-04: allow ROC Eastman (Recreation Opportunities for Children) to hold up to four book-sale fundraisers a year at 110 Industrial Road
for: Michael Zwaagstra; Jac Siemens; Susan Penner; Bill Hiebert; Earl Funk
reasons_against: Zoning: retail does not belong in the light-industrial park, and the conditions could not stop the use changing; not opposition to the charity.

what: Second reading of By-Law 2241: rezoning for a 3-storey apartment beside Bethesda hospital (health-worker guest suite and seniors' access cited in favour)

what: Variance for the Steinbach Housing seniors’ complex: seven storeys with 1:1 parking

what: Variance for six-storey Bridgepark Manor seniors’ building with 1.25 parking per unit
